title: spec: ConnectorConnectionState.status JSDoc says reconnect_required means only that the authorization server refused the grant; since PR #28598 a discovery refusal of the connection token sets it too
body:
domain:server#3 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5kE5BrPUPNMMyv6oCH

Filing gate: ① a published-text defect owed by landed work (PR #28598, `Part of #26702`). That PR's Acceptance notes name it; the server seat may not edit `packages/spec`, so it is filed for the spec lane. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets the lane and grade.
reach: the published `.d.ts` of `@objectstack/spec` carries the JSDoc of `ConnectorConnectionState.status` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` (read at `origin/main`, the `reconnect_required` bullet above the `status` member): "`reconnect_required` — the authorization server refused the grant." After PR #28598, `service-automation` also sets `reconnect_required` (through the store's existing `markReconnectRequired`) when the upstream refuses the connection's borrowed token at MCP tool discovery, with a platform sentence in `statusReason`.

**Business reason.** An app author or agent reading the contract to decide what a `reconnect_required` connection means is told only half of it, and may tell the admin the wrong remedy (re-grant versus reconnect after the vendor revoked the token's access).

**Reader who acts:** the `domain:spec` seat, a one-sentence JSDoc edit (no shape change: `Clause-②: no`, `skip-changeset` or a spec `patch` changeset as the lane rules).

**Dedupe:** `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue reconnect_required JSDoc` and `ConnectorConnectionState status reconnect_required` → no open card with this text.

## Wanted

The bullet reads, in substance: the grant stopped working, either because the authorization server refused it on refresh, or because the upstream refused the connection's token at discovery; `statusReason` says which.

Links: PR #28598, #26702, the reading 6553121554.
